obligation: CPNI breach notice to law enforcement (current rule)
trigger: Reasonable determination that a person, without or exceeding authorization, intentionally gained access to, used, or disclosed CPNI (64.2011(e)); in this scenario, confirmed reads of the CDR store by a compromised adapter account
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination (internal target 2 business days)
notify: USSS and FBI electronically through the FCC central reporting facility (link at fcc.gov/eb/cpni)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each operating carrier subsidiary whose customers' CPNI is involved (64.2003(o)); no size exemption

obligation: CPNI breach: hold on customer and public disclosure
trigger: Law enforcement notice filed
deadline: No customer notice or public disclosure until 7 full business days after the USSS and FBI notice, notwithstanding contrary state law. Earlier customer notice only if the carrier flags an extraordinarily urgent need in its notice and consults the investigating agency; the agency may direct a delay of up to 30 days, extendable in writing
notify: Hold; log any agency direction (the agency logs it on the reporting facility)

obligation: CPNI breach notice to customers (current rule)
trigger: Law enforcement notice process complete
deadline: After the hold ends (or as the agency directs); the current rule sets no further outer deadline, so plan to the state clocks below
notify: Each customer whose CPNI was breached; enterprise and government accounts through their account representatives

trigger: Any breach discovered
deadline: Record kept at least 2 years: dates of discovery and notification, description of the CPNI, circumstances

obligation: CPNI and covered data breach notice (2023 amendments; NOT yet effective)
citation: 47 CFR 64.2011 as amended by FCC 23-111 (89 FR 9968); upheld in Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC (6th Cir. 2025-08-13)
trigger: Would cover inadvertent as well as intentional access, and customer PII as well as CPNI
deadline: Would require FCC, USSS, and FBI notice within 7 business days; customer notice without unreasonable delay and within 30 days after reasonable determination; breaches under 500 customers with no reasonably likely harm in an annual summary
applies_at_this_tier: No - amendments remain delayed indefinitely; no FCC effective-date notice in the Federal Register through 2026-10-05. Recheck at every incident

trigger: Opt-out mechanisms fail so that customers' inability to opt out is more than an anomaly (for example, BSS approval flags corrupted during the incident)
deadline: Written notice within 5 business days

obligation: Annual CPNI certification after the incident
trigger: Next certification after an incident
deadline: By March 1, covering the prior year: the explanation of operating procedures must be accurate, with actions taken against data brokers and a summary of customer complaints about unauthorized release of CPNI

trigger: Any compromise of a lawful interception or of call-identifying information to unauthorized persons, or any unlawful electronic surveillance on company premises
deadline: Within a reasonable time upon discovery
notify: Affected law enforcement agencies (contacts in each subsidiary's SSI appendix)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the lawful-intercept enclave, an AQ intercept function, or intercept records were reached or cannot be ruled out

trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility, including one caused by containment (for example, isolating an SBC cluster)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery, by telephone and in writing electronically; first follow-up no later than 2 hours after initial contact, then as new material information becomes available
notify: Designated outage contacts at each potentially affected PSAP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - wireline and interconnected VoIP provider

trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 988 special facility
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery; first follow-up no later than 2 hours after initial contact
notify: Designated contacts at the affected 988 special facility

trigger: Wireline outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects 900,000 user minutes, affects 667 OC3 minutes, affects special offices and facilities, or potentially affects a 911 or 988 special facility
deadline: Notification within 120 minutes of discovery; Initial Communications Outage Report within 72 hours; Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days

obligation: FCC outage report (interconnected VoIP, including SL-2)
trigger: VoIP outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects a 911 or 988 special facility; or 900,000 user minutes with complete loss of service; or special offices and facilities
deadline: Notification within 240 minutes (911 or 988 facility) or 24 hours (other triggers); Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 630,000 VoIP lines and SL-2 seats

obligation: FCC outage report (SS7 and LEC tandem)
trigger: SS7 outage of at least 30 minutes with at least 90,000 blocked calls (real-time) or 30,000 lost calls (historic), or MTP message surrogates; tandem outages of at least 30 minutes with 90,000 blocked calls or 667 OC3-minutes lost
deadline: Notification within 120 minutes of discovery (SS7); Initial and Final reports per 4.9 and 4.11
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SS7 provider for 14 rural carriers; LEC tandem operator

trigger: FCC activates DIRS for the service area during the incident (for example, a hurricane)
deadline: Daily infrastructure status reports from activation until deactivation

trigger: Any severity-1 incident or any incident that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery; the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours (POL-03 4.7)
notify: Internal (disclosure committee minute with date and time)

trigger: Committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination

trigger: The incident is also a CPNI breach and 64.2011(b)(1) bars public disclosure
deadline: Item 1.05 disclosure may be delayed for the 64.2011(b)(1) period, in no event more than seven business days after the USSS and FBI notice, if the company notifies the SEC by EDGAR correspondence no later than the date the 8-K was otherwise due. Does not cover an agency-directed extension under 64.2011(b)(3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is subject to 47 CFR 64.2011
clock_starts: Materiality determination (original due date) and the USSS and FBI notice (cap)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05(c) Attorney General delay
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date, with further periods only on further Attorney General determinations
notify: SEC (through the Department of Justice); request made through outside counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the investigating agency seeks a delay beyond the CPNI hold

trigger: Required information was not determined or was unavailable at filing
deadline: Amendment within 4 business days after the information is determined or becomes available

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Next Form 10-K
deadline: With the annual report; describe whether incidents materially affected or are reasonably likely to affect the company

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information as each state defines it (often a name with an SSN, account credentials, or financial account data; call detail alone may not qualify; counsel decides per state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); the 64.2011(b)(1) hold applies notwithstanding contrary state law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - customers in FL, GA, SC, NC and seasonal or former residents of other states

obligation: State attorney general, regulator, and consumer reporting agency notices
trigger: State-set thresholds of affected residents
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or regulators where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check each state in counsel's matrix (updated within 12 months, STD-03.2)

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (for example, portal user names with passwords or security answers; SSN, financial account, or government ID with a name)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred; delay only on a law enforcement agency's written request (4)(b); notice under the primary or functional federal regulator's rules is deemed compliant (4)(g)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida-defined personal information is involved (worked example)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (a timely copy of a federal-regulator notice is deemed compliant, 501.171(4)(g))

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the company relies on the exception

trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (care vendors, chatbot vendor, bill print vendor) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determination (company contracts require 24 hours)
notify: The company (Director of Third-Party Risk Management)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering an extortion payment (for example, to suppress publication of stolen call detail)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule published as of 2026-10-05. Voluntary report to CISA and FBI on day 0-2 instead

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during contract performance (for example, found in an acquired network during recovery)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal contracts include the clause

trigger: A covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) identified in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal contracts include the clause

trigger: A covered article subject to a FASCSA order identified during performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal contracts include the clause

obligation: Enterprise, government, and wholesale customer contract notices
citation: Customer contracts (1,900 enterprise and government accounts; federal agency contracts; 64 wholesale and 14 SS7 customers)
trigger: Security incident affecting the customer's CPNI, data, or services
deadline: Per contract; customer notice of a CPNI breach still waits for the 64.2011(b) hold unless the investigating agency agrees

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 business customer notices
citation: Service agreements and SOC 2 system description commitments (P09)
trigger: Incident affecting managed network or hosted UC customers' data or service
deadline: Per service agreement (most require notice within 24 hours of confirmation)
notify: SL-1 and SL-2 customer security contacts
owner: Vice President, Managed Services; Vice President, Unified Communications

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
